cosy-lesson.title: My Life With & My Life Without Hearing Abilities

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Auditory ≠ Visual – relating to the sense of hearing.

p.em: Example: Auditory processing helps us interpret music and speech.

cosy-blockquote.p: Acoustics ≠ Muffledness – the properties or qualities of a room or building that determine how sound is transmitted.

p.em: Example: The acoustics in the cathedral made the choir sound magnificent.

cosy-blockquote.p: Decibel ≠ Silence – a unit used to measure the intensity of a sound.

p.em: Example: Concerts often reach loud decibel levels.

cosy-blockquote.p: Tinnitus ≠ Clarity – ringing or buzzing in the ears.

p.em: Example: Constant tinnitus can make sleeping difficult.

cosy-blockquote.p: Impairment ≠ Full capability – the state or fact of being impaired or damaged.

p.em: Example: Hearing impairment affects millions of people worldwide.

cosy-blockquote.p: Sensory ≠ Numb – relating to sensation or the physical senses.

p.em: Example: A walk in the forest offers rich sensory stimulation.

cosy-blockquote.p: Vibration ≠ Stillness – a continuous rapid oscillation or shaking motion.

p.em: Example: Deaf dancers feel the rhythmic vibration of the bass.

cosy-blockquote.p: Subtitled ≠ Uncaptioned – provided with captions translating or transcribing the dialogue.

p.em: Example: Watching subtitled films helps with language learning.

cosy-blockquote.p: Overstimulation ≠ Calm – excessive stimulation of the senses.

p.em: Example: Urban noise pollution causes auditory overstimulation.

cosy-blockquote.p: Silence ≠ Noise – complete absence of sound.

p.em: Example: Finding moments of silence restores mental peace.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
How does city noise pollution impact our long-term auditory health?
★ How noisy is your daily living environment?

What role do subtitled media play in accessibility for people with hearing impairment?
★ Do you prefer watching movies with subtitles turned on?

How do people experiencing tinnitus cope with loud ambient sound?
★ Have you ever experienced temporary ringing in your ears after a concert?

Why is tactile vibration important in sign language and deaf performing arts?
★ How do you respond to ambient rhythm and acoustic music?

Does urban overstimulation make intentional silence more valuable today?
★ Where do you go when you want complete quiet?

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
How might advancements in hearing aid technology eliminate severe hearing impairment?
★ How do you think medical technology will improve human senses in 20 years?

Why is designing buildings with proper acoustics essential for public accessibility?
★ What is your favorite quiet architectural spot?

How does losing one sensory channel alter a person's perception of space?
★ If you had to spend 24 hours without sound, what would you miss most?

Should cities enforce maximum decibel limits in residential quarters at night?
★ What quiet hours rules exist in your neighborhood?

How can society build more inclusive environments for the deaf community?
★ Have you ever learned any sign language phrases?
